# Compute-unit notes — verified_inference

Localnet CU measurements from `anchor test` (the table below is rewritten by
the test suite's `after()` hook on every green run). Devnet numbers matter
later (P2+): re-measure there before doing the mainnet fee projection —
localnet and devnet CU should match for the same binary, but verify.

## Measured CU (localnet)

<!-- CU:BEGIN (auto-generated by anchor test) -->

Measured 2026-07-16T16:22:25.280Z on localnet (anchor test).

| instruction | CU consumed | tx message bytes |
|---|---|---|
| register_attestation | 8391 | 351 |
| post_receipt (ed25519 + program ix) | 11941 | 634 |
| post_receipt (2nd, steady-state) | 13441 | 634 |
| post_receipt_batch (32 receipts) | 11756 | 513 |
| verify_inference_proof (stub) | 8961 | 244 |

Batched amortization: 32 receipts in one batch -> 367.4 CU/receipt vs 11941 CU for a single post_receipt.

<!-- CU:END -->

Notes on the numbers:

- Run-to-run variance of ~±1.5k CU on the receipt instructions comes from PDA
  bump grinding: tests generate a fresh random enclave keypair each run, and
  `find_program_address` / on-chain seed validation cost depends on how many
  bump candidates get tried for those seeds. Expect the same spread on devnet;
  report CU as a distribution, not a single number.
- `post_receipt` / `post_receipt_batch` CU are the **program** CU only. The
  ed25519 precompile instruction that precedes them is priced by the runtime
  per-signature (ed25519 verify = 1 extra signature's flat fee, currently
  5,000 lamports/sig) and does **not** show up in `computeUnitsConsumed`.
  For fee projection: batched vs single differs in (a) one tx + one signature
  per N receipts instead of per 1, (b) one rent-exempt account per N instead
  of per 1 — that dominates the economics, not the CU delta.
- Account rent (devnet == mainnet): AttestationAccount 8+265=273 B,
  ReceiptAccount 8+153=161 B, ReceiptBatchAccount 8+125=133 B,
  ProofRecordAccount 8+107=115 B (Anchor InitSpace; String max_len 64).
- `verify_inference_proof` is a stub (records hashes only). Real Groth16 via
  alt_bn128 syscalls is expected around ~200k CU (Light Protocol's
  groth16-solana ballpark) — measure when wired in P3/P4, do not use the stub
  number for projections.

## Toolchain resolution (what fought and how it was pinned)

- Installed toolchain: `anchor-cli 1.0.2` (avm), `solana-cli 4.0.0-rc.0`
  (Agave), rustc 1.89.0 pinned via `rust-toolchain.toml` (scaffold default).
- `Anchor.toml` pins `anchor_version = "1.0.2"`; the program crate declares
  `anchor-lang = "1.0.2"`, which cargo resolves to the semver-compatible
  1.1.2 (fine — Anchor 1.x is stable API).
- Anchor 1.x no longer re-exports the full `solana_program` facade. The
  instructions-sysvar introspection helpers (`load_current_index_checked`,
  `load_instruction_at_checked`) and the ed25519 program id had to be taken
  from the modular SDK crates directly: `solana-instructions-sysvar = "3.0.0"`
  and `solana-sdk-ids = "3.1.0"` (same versions anchor-lang itself uses, so
  no duplicate-crate conflicts).
- TS side: Anchor 1.x renamed the npm package `@coral-xyz/anchor` ->
  `@anchor-lang/core` (same API, still on `@solana/web3.js` 1.x, so
  `Ed25519Program.createInstructionWithPublicKey` works as before).
- `yarn` is not installed on this machine; `Anchor.toml` sets
  `package_manager = "npm"` and the test script uses `npx ts-mocha`.
- groth16: dependency intentionally NOT added yet (P0). When wiring it,
  start from Light Protocol's `groth16-solana` crate (alt_bn128 syscalls)
  — see TODO(groth16) markers in
  `programs/verified_inference/src/instructions/verify_inference_proof.rs`
  and `src/state.rs`.
